newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope ushers in Christmas, prays for non-believers.
newsitem.headline: Pope ushers in Christmas, prays for non-believers.

text.p: Pope John Paul led the world's 960 million Roman Catholics into Christmas on Wednesday and prayed for peace and joy for believers and non-believers alike.
The 76-year-old Pontiff, who has suffered from a series of health problems in recent years, celebrated a solemn midnight mass in St Peter's Basilica, the largest church in Christendom.
"We pray today for everyone, Christians and non-Christians, believers and non-believers alike," he said in his sermon.

"I send everyone a cordial greeting and I pray that this source of joy issuing forth in human history with the birth of the Son of God will be plentiful for all, so that each person may draw from it and quench his thirst," he said.
The Pope, wearing resplendent gold and white vestments, appeared to be in relatively good form during the service, reading his sermon in a strong voice.

But, heeding medical advice to conserve his strength, the Polish Pontiff will skip the Christmas day mass in the Basilica later on Wednesday morning. The decison was announced by the Vatican two weeks ago.
The fact that the Pope will miss a traditional celebration of the Christian liturgical calendar again underscored that old age is taking its toll on his stamina.

The Pope will, however, deliver his "Urbi et Orbi" message and blessing from the basilica's central balcony to crowds gathered in the square below at 1100 GMT on Wednesday and read holiday greetings in some 50 languages.
Celebrating the day mass as well as the midnight mass would have forced the Pope -- an early riser -- to get just a few hours sleep.
When he left hospital in October after an appendix operation -- his latest health problem -- doctors told him to rest more.
The Pope dedicated his homily at the midnight mass to the Biblical story of Christ's birth. "To us a child is born, to us a son is given," he said, quoting the prophet Isaiah.
During the mass, the congregation recited prayers in Arabic, Portuguese, Italian, Polish, German, and Tagalog, spoken in the Philippines.
One of the prayers of the faithful during the midnight mass, televised to some 60 countries, was for children in the world who are "violated in their human dignity".
Another was that world leaders and diplomats would be "men and women of peace and work for understanding and justice in freedom."
The Pope's health has been in the spotlight for the past four years.

A year ago, he had to skip the Christmas Day mass when he was taken ill during the night after he celebrated midnight mass. He later had to interrupt his "Urbi et Orbi" address on live television when he felt ill again as he was reading it.

His health began deteriorating in 1992, when doctors removed a colon tumour that was starting to turn malignant. In 1993 he was hospitalised for a dislocated shoulder and in 1994 he underwent bone replacement surgery after breaking his femur.
He is due to go to the papal summer residence at Castelgandolfo just south of Rome from Dec 26 to Dec 31 for a period of rest.
